channel.title: The Tipsy Professor
channel.description: Essays written between the second drink and the third. Mostly about elsewhere, occasionally about being wrong.

item.title: Against Cairns
item.description: In praise of leaving a place exactly as unmarked as you found it, argued badly by a man who has built several.

item.title: The Trouble With Best
item.description: A statistician who ranks people for a living explains why she distrusts every ranking she has ever produced, including the ones she is proud of.

item.title: The Comedian Asks Better Questions
item.description: Why a stand-up with no press pass gets further with a historian in one sitting than most interviewers manage in a career.

item.title: The Harbour Was a Rumour
item.description: Three nights in Reykjavík, awake for most of them, learning that a place will not introduce itself until you have stopped expecting it to.

item.title: Two People Disagree About Stalker
item.description: A hundred and sixty-one minutes of men walking slowly through a wet field, watched with someone who loves it, by someone who did not.

item.title: The Papaya Rows
item.description: Four hours in a plantation in Kerala, doing nothing useful, with a man who had no interest in explaining anything to me.

item.title: Overheard at the Laundromat, Lisbon
item.description: A forty-minute wash cycle, two strangers, and the strongest argument for eavesdropping I have encountered in some years.

item.title: On Being Drawn
item.description: Someone made pictures of me for a year. What I learned is unflattering, and not about my face.

item.title: On Losing Arguments in Four Scripts
item.description: Being wrong in your own language is embarrassing. Being wrong in someone else’s is an education, and cheaper than most.

item.title: The Night Window
item.description: A twenty-four-hour place in Osaka, three people who did not know each other, and the best conversation I have ever failed to follow.

item.title: A Proof That the Best Coffee Is Always the Second Cup
item.description: Rigorous in form, indefensible in substance, and correct. A short paper for anyone who has ever been disappointed by a cup they had been looking forward to.

item.title: Warm Water
item.description: On distrusting pleasant places, a prejudice I held for eleven years and gave up in about forty minutes.

item.title: Against the Highlight Reel
item.description: An argument with the way we have all agreed to describe our own lives, conducted mostly against myself, and lost in the usual places.

item.title: The Last One Outside
item.description: A short defence of standing in the cold with strangers, written by someone who does not smoke and keeps going out anyway.

item.title: Seventeen Things I Do Instead of Sleeping
item.description: An inventory, offered without defence, by someone who has read all the advice and follows roughly none of it.
